roles.title: Help Desk / IT Support
roles.tagline: Broadest on-ramp. A+ validates the basics; local market determines whether it's the right first step.
roles.entry_note: Sometimes the right strategic move depending on local market. High volume of postings, genuine exposure to tickets/hardware/AD. Don't overlook it because it feels unglamorous.
roles.description: The broadest entry ramp into IT, covering technical support for end users across hardware, software, and connectivity issues. High volume of job postings and genuine exposure to ticketing systems, Active Directory, and hardware troubleshooting makes this a legitimate foundation for multiple career paths.
what_they_do: Respond to user tickets and walk-ins for hardware and software issues
Manage user accounts and permissions in Active Directory or Azure AD
Image and configure new workstations and laptops
Escalate complex issues to Tier 2 and document resolutions in a ticketing system
Support VPN, printers, peripherals, and productivity software (M365, Google Workspace)
requirements: CompTIA A+ certification (or actively pursuing it)
Basic understanding of Windows OS and networking fundamentals
High school diploma or associate's degree — bachelor's is helpful but not required at entry
Strong communication and problem-solving skills

next_moves.title: NOC Technician
next_moves.why: Network+ earned at Help Desk tier is the direct credential gate. Many NOC postings explicitly list Help Desk experience as qualifying, and the troubleshooting skills transfer directly.

next_moves.title: Cloud Support Associate
next_moves.why: AWS CCP or AZ-900 can be earned while working Help Desk. Cloud vendors actively recruit from Help Desk queues for Tier 1 cloud support positions.

next_moves.title: GRC Analyst T1
next_moves.why: Help Desk exposure to compliance policies, access control tickets, and IT governance creates a natural bridge into risk and audit work — especially once you add Security+.

tiers.label: ENTRY

required_certs.name: CompTIA A+
required_certs.cost_note: Per exam voucher (2 exams required = ~$506 total). Prices as of 2025.

tiers.education_bar: No degree required; associate's degree helpful. Many employers list degree as preferred, not required at this tier.

branch_rationale.noc-technician: Network+ earned at Help Desk tier is the primary credential gate for NOC roles; many job postings explicitly list prior Help Desk experience as qualifying.
branch_rationale.cloud-support: AWS CCP / AZ-900 can be added while at Help Desk; several cloud vendors explicitly recruit from Help Desk for their Tier 1 cloud support queues.

tiers.label: MID

required_certs.name: CompTIA Network+
required_certs.cost_note: Single exam voucher, 2025 pricing.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's degree increasingly expected; associate's + experience is a common path.

tiers.label: SENIOR

required_certs.name: CompTIA Security+
required_certs.cost_note: Single exam voucher, 2025 pricing.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's in CS, IT, or related field standard at this level.

roles.title: NOC Technician
roles.tagline: Network operations monitoring. Network+ is the direct qualifier.
roles.entry_note: Shift work is common. Strong exposure to real network infrastructure, alerting tools, and escalation workflows — legitimate foundation for network engineering.
roles.description: Network Operations Center technicians monitor the health of network infrastructure around the clock, responding to alerts, escalating outages, and maintaining documentation. Shift work is standard but the hands-on exposure to real routing, switching, and monitoring tools is a proven foundation for network engineering careers.
what_they_do: Monitor network dashboards for alerts, anomalies, and outages across 24/7 shifts
Respond to circuit outages, device failures, and threshold breaches
Open and manage trouble tickets with ISPs and hardware vendors
Run and document incident escalations to Tier 2 / Network Engineering
Maintain device logs, change control records, and operational runbooks
requirements: CompTIA Network+
Familiarity with OSI model, TCP/IP, VLANs, and basic routing concepts
Associate's degree or equivalent; bachelor's preferred
Experience with monitoring tools (PRTG, SolarWinds, Nagios, or Zabbix) is a strong plus

next_moves.title: Junior Network Admin
next_moves.why: NOC operations experience is explicitly cited as qualifying in junior network admin postings. The escalation path from reactive monitoring to proactive configuration work is well-defined and expected.

next_moves.title: SOC Analyst T1
next_moves.why: Network visibility skills from NOC work — packet analysis, firewall log review, traffic anomaly detection — translate directly to SOC Tier 1 alert triage with Security+ in hand.

tiers.label: ENTRY

required_certs.name: CompTIA Network+
required_certs.cost_note: Single exam voucher, 2025 pricing.

tiers.education_bar: No degree required in many postings; associate's or bachelor's preferred.

salary_range.source_label: BLS OES — Computer Network Support Specialists (May 2024)

branch_rationale.junior-network-admin: NOC experience is explicitly cited as qualifying experience for Junior Network Admin postings; the operational exposure to routing, switching, and monitoring tools is directly transferable.

tiers.label: MID

required_certs.name: Cisco CCNA
required_certs.cost_note: Single exam (200-301), $300 USD. Register at Pearson VUE. Verified 2025.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's in networking or IT increasingly expected.

salary_range.source_label: BLS OOH — Network & Computer Systems Administrators (May 2024)

tiers.label: SENIOR

required_certs.name: Cisco CCNP Enterprise
required_certs.cost_note: $400 ENCOR core exam (350-401) + $300 concentration exam. Total $700. Verified at Pearson VUE 2025.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's standard; master's in some enterprise orgs.

salary_range.source_label: BLS OOH — Network & Computer Systems Administrators (May 2024)

roles.title: Cloud Support Associate
roles.tagline: Vendor-side or third-party cloud Tier 1 support. AWS CCP / AZ-900 is the entry gate.
roles.entry_note: AWS and Azure both hire at this level with just a foundational cert. Direct path into cloud engineering with consistent cert progression.
roles.description: Cloud Support Associates handle Tier 1 technical support for cloud platform customers or internal engineering teams, resolving provisioning errors, access issues, and service disruptions. AWS and Azure actively recruit at this level with only a foundational cert, making it one of the most accessible entry points into cloud engineering.
what_they_do: Respond to customer or internal tickets on cloud services (EC2, S3, IAM, VPC, Azure resources)
Troubleshoot cloud resource provisioning failures, permission errors, and connectivity issues
Escalate complex infrastructure problems to cloud engineering teams
Document resolutions and write runbooks for recurring failure patterns
Monitor cloud dashboards and flag cost anomalies or service degradation
requirements: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner (CCP) or Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900)
Basic understanding of cloud concepts: IaaS, PaaS, regions, availability zones, IAM
No degree required for many postings; bachelor's preferred
Scripting basics (Bash, Python) are a growing expectation even at entry level

next_moves.title: SOC Analyst T1
next_moves.why: Cloud security monitoring exposure — CloudTrail, GuardDuty, Azure Sentinel — builds skills directly applicable to SOC Tier 1 alert triage. Add Security+ and the pivot is clean.

next_moves.title: GRC Analyst T1
next_moves.why: Cloud compliance work (SOC 2, FedRAMP, AWS Config rules, Azure Policy) creates a natural bridge into GRC and audit roles. Many GRC teams are short on cloud-savvy analysts.

tiers.label: ENTRY

required_certs.name: AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner
required_certs.cost_note: Exam fee as of 2025. Register at aws.training.

required_certs.name: Microsoft Azure Fundamentals (AZ-900)
required_certs.cost_note: Exam fee as of 2025. Register via Pearson VUE or Certiport.

tiers.education_bar: No degree required for many cloud support roles; bachelor's preferred.

tiers.label: MID

required_certs.name: AWS Certified SysOps Administrator – Associate
required_certs.cost_note: Exam fee as of 2025.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's in CS, IT, or cloud-adjacent increasingly standard.

salary_range.source_label: BLS OOH — Network & Computer Systems Administrators (May 2024)

tiers.label: SENIOR

required_certs.name: AWS Certified Solutions Architect – Professional
required_certs.cost_note: Exam fee as of 2025.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's standard; strong portfolio can substitute.

roles.title: GRC / IT Audit Analyst T1
roles.tagline: Governance, risk, and compliance. Security+ + BA degree is the common entry combination.
roles.entry_note: One of the few IT tracks where a non-technical bachelor's (accounting, business, poli-sci) is a genuine advantage. Heavy documentation and framework work (NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2).
roles.description: Governance, Risk, and Compliance analysts ensure IT systems meet regulatory and policy requirements across frameworks like NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2, and FedRAMP. Unlike most IT tracks, a non-technical bachelor's is a genuine advantage here — accounting, business, and policy backgrounds all map well.
what_they_do: Audit IT systems and controls against NIST, ISO 27001, SOC 2, CMMC, or FedRAMP requirements
Write and maintain policies, procedures, risk registers, and control documentation
Conduct control testing and document findings for internal and external audit cycles
Coordinate with IT and security teams on remediation timelines and evidence collection
Support external auditors, regulators, and FedRAMP assessors with evidence packages
requirements: CompTIA Security+
Bachelor's degree — any field works; accounting, business, CS, or poli-sci are all relevant
Familiarity with at least one compliance framework (NIST 800-53, SOC 2, ISO 27001)
Strong writing and documentation skills — this role is documentation-intensive

next_moves.title: SOC Analyst T1
next_moves.why: GRC analysts who add SIEM exposure and network monitoring skills can pivot into SOC roles. The deep knowledge of control failures and policy gaps is additive to threat detection work.

tiers.label: ENTRY

required_certs.name: CompTIA Security+
required_certs.cost_note: Single exam voucher, 2025 pricing.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's degree common (any field); accounting, business, or IT preferred. BA is more commonly a real requirement here than in other entry tracks.

tiers.label: MID

required_certs.name: ISACA CISA (Certified Information Systems Auditor)
required_certs.cost_note: ISACA member exam fee as of 2025. Non-member: $760. Verify at isaca.org.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's required; master's increasingly common at mid-level in financial services and healthcare.

tiers.label: SENIOR

required_certs.name: ISACA CRISC (Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control)
required_certs.cost_note: ISACA member exam fee as of 2025. Verify at isaca.org.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's required; master's common. CISSP sometimes listed as senior bar.

roles.title: SOC Analyst T1
roles.tagline: Defensive security monitoring. Entry is real but competitive — most postings still prefer prior IT experience.
roles.entry_note: Honest caveat: despite T1 labeling, many SOC postings request 1–2 years of IT or security experience. Your Network+ + Security+ combo with a degree puts you in the running, but homelab evidence (SIEM configs, detection rules) will separate you from other applicants. Don't assume the cert alone is sufficient.
roles.description: Security Operations Center analysts monitor SIEM alerts and investigate potential threats in real time. Despite T1 labeling, most SOC postings want 1–2 years of IT or security experience. Your degree plus Network+ and Security+ is competitive, but demonstrable homelab work — SIEM configurations, detection rules, CTF completions — is what separates applications.
what_they_do: Triage and investigate SIEM alerts from Splunk, Elastic, or Microsoft Sentinel
Analyze logs from firewalls, EDR tools, email gateways, and cloud platforms
Escalate confirmed incidents to Tier 2 analysts and incident response teams
Document findings in ticketing systems and contribute to SOC runbooks
Perform initial malware triage, phishing analysis, and IOC lookups
requirements: CompTIA Security+ (minimum); CySA+ is a strong differentiator
Bachelor's degree in CS, cybersecurity, or IT
Homelab or lab environment evidence strongly recommended (TryHackMe, HackTheBox, self-built SIEM)
Familiarity with Splunk, Microsoft Sentinel, or comparable SIEM platform

next_moves.title: GRC Analyst T1
next_moves.why: SOC incident investigation gives you hands-on knowledge of control failures and security gaps — a natural pivot into GRC and compliance work, especially with audit skills added.

tiers.label: ENTRY

required_certs.name: CompTIA Security+
required_certs.cost_note: Single exam voucher, 2025 pricing.

required_certs.name: CompTIA CySA+ (recommended, not always required)
required_certs.cost_note: Single exam voucher, 2025 pricing. Often listed as preferred, not required.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's in CS, cybersecurity, or IT is common. Degree + Security+ is the minimum credible package for most employers.

tiers.label: MID

required_certs.name: CompTIA CySA+
required_certs.cost_note: Single exam voucher, 2025 pricing.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's standard. Active SIEM and EDR tool experience increasingly expected.

tiers.label: SENIOR

required_certs.name: GIAC GCIA or GCIH
required_certs.cost_note: Exam fee as of 2025. Includes two practice tests. Verify at giac.org.

tiers.education_bar: Bachelor's standard. SANS/GIAC certs carry significant weight at this tier.

ai_branch.title: AI Security Engineer
ai_branch.note: Senior-only branch. Requires deep SOC experience + LLM/ML security knowledge. Not a realistic entry or mid-tier destination.

roles.title: Junior Network Admin
roles.tagline: Hands-on network configuration and maintenance. Homelab is table stakes.
roles.entry_note: Honest caveat: postings often expect hands-on lab or home lab experience with Cisco gear even at junior level. Your Network+ is necessary but not sufficient — build a homelab (GNS3, Packet Tracer, or physical gear) before applying. Competition from candidates with prior NOC or Help Desk experience is real.
roles.description: Junior network administrators configure, maintain, and troubleshoot network equipment including switches, routers, and firewalls under senior engineer supervision. The 'junior' label is misleading — most postings expect demonstrated hands-on lab experience with Cisco gear. Network+ is necessary but not sufficient without a homelab to back it up.
what_they_do: Configure and maintain Cisco switches and routers under senior engineer supervision
Implement VLANs, ACLs, and basic firewall rule sets
Troubleshoot Layer 1–3 connectivity issues across the organization
Document network topology changes and maintain device inventories
Monitor network performance metrics and respond to alerts alongside senior engineers
requirements: CompTIA Network+
Homelab experience with GNS3, Packet Tracer, or physical Cisco gear — this is a real expectation
Bachelor's in networking or IT preferred; associate's + strong homelab can substitute at smaller orgs
Basic Cisco IOS command familiarity is expected even at junior level

next_moves.title: NOC Technician
next_moves.why: If junior network admin postings prove too competitive, NOC is a proven lateral move that leads to the same mid-level network engineering track — often faster due to volume of NOC openings.

next_moves.title: SOC Analyst T1
next_moves.why: Network visibility experience — packet analysis, firewall log review, intrusion detection — translates directly to SOC Tier 1 alert work, especially with Security+ already in hand.
